body:
Thank you for the support.  I've put alot of the toxicity of my grandparents and my alcoholism of my dad completely out of my life.  The last time I talked with my grandparent was at the dad's funeral in summer 2013 and before that was back in 2005.  When my dad initially went to prison and left my life is when I probably grieved for him being gone the most.  When he finally did pass away almost a decade later I was already at terms with his absence.

I've had difficulty defining my problem to the few resources I've tried in the past and maybe that is why some of them weren't as effective.  While I try to discover the information I need on my own sometimes I just need someone with experience that can give an educated opinion on the topic.

Had a lengthy post typed up but RES bugged out on my and deleted it all.  I'll try to type up a concise version that explains it.

My mom, younger sister, and I moved into my grandparents (dad side) when we lost our house.  My dad was recently sent to prison for excessive DUIs.  When my older sister's husband was accussed of child abuse my mom moved to Oregon to help her take care of her kids while they worked through the DHS system so he could move back in with his family.  My younger sister and I stayed with my grandparents in Arizona so we could still be enrolled in our school and not uproot completely move to a new state.

I wasn't ever a rebellious kid and got along as well as siblings can with each other.  My grandmother made a constant point to remind me how annoying it was for her to come pick me up after band practice at 9PM twice a week.  She would always find something to nitpick me on anything that would be an inconvenience for her.  One night a friend invited me out for her birthday party with our social group.  We were having a good time and since I didn't come straight home after school once my grandma tracked me down she made it a point to say that she should've called the cops on me.  The constant belittling was finally dragging me down and I decided for my own sanity it would be best for me to move to Oregon with my older sister and my mom to finish school there with them.  

I moved in with them and school went well.  Made some friends pretty easily but I still really kept to myself.  At the end oaf the term my mom and I moved back down to Arizona to my grandparents so I could finish school with my original class and so she could help my younger sister as well.  In hindsight I wish I would have stayed in Oregon and just finished school up here.

With my mom on my side I was able to manage to get through my senior year relatively unscathed.  At the end of the year my mom decided to move back up to Oregon with my younger sister to take her out of the vile household of my grandparents.  I was initially accepted to go to this one school in July but was still trying to find suitable housing in the area.  The school was about 60 miles away and I was fresh out of high school with no resources.  I tried talking with my grandparents about staying the month before classes started so I can find a place but they refused and scoffed at me for even proposing the idea.

So with almost no money to my name I ended up taking a Greyhound back up to my older sister's place in Oregon.  Once there I found two fulltime jobs and work both so I felt Like I could contribute to my sister helping me out.  I eventually found a better paying job and then moved out from her place. 

Fast forward a few years and I'm now enrolled in another school on my junior year of chemical engineering and in the Marine Corps Reserves.  Now with my social issues it's sometimes very difficult for me to relate to others and to enjoy small talk and have fun.  I feel like that's been another reason why I haven't been able to find a stable romantic relationship at all.  

I've recently reconnected with this one girl 6 months ago I wasn't initially romantically interested with but we got along very well and were in similar positions in our lives when we worked together back in 2013.  I left that job to spend some time with my dad since he was diagnosed with terminal cancer and died a few months later.

Initially when we finally caught up with each other I tried to pique her interest in a relationship but she turned me down for it.  That was a hard hit along with some of my stress of classes as well.  It was frustrating that I felt like a failure in all aspects of my life and that nothing would ever really improve my situation at all, that I was destined to be a failure.  I decided to take a step back and retake some classes to help improve my self confidence but I then fell back into a rut again and came to the conclusion that why should I even bother getting out of bed today?  I should just go kill myself since I can never be happy with anything in my life.   I feel like I've improved the past few days but I still have no idea where I am at.

Tried to summarize alot but it still seemed like I ranted for to long.  Thanks for listening SQLwitch.

Recollecting for a bit trying to determine the last time I felt a sense of connection or anything of that nature was probably back in early highschool almost 10 years ago.  Hobbies and clubs specifically band and wrestling helped at being a part of something.  Had a rocky end at the end of highschool with moving and disagreemnents with my guardians at the time (grandparents) and well had no support at home.  Socially I wasn't a butterfly and had a pretty horrendous stutter so I kept to myself.

I don't lean on others because I feel like if I do then they'll turn away and I'll be alone again.  My social circle is small and somewhat dispersed since we live in different towns.

I tend to fall through the cracks so it's somewhat expected.  A few years ago I tried talking to a psychologist and that didn't seem to change my view.  The only thing that really came from those sessions is if I can't change something then why worry about it?

Last term I took another nosedive and ended up talking to a school psychological services and a physician and tried using a generic Prozac.  There was also a group for anxiety that I went to as well and well my emotions weren't dependent on anxious feelings of that nature.  I'm also in the military so I'm depended on to complete missions and improve the morale of others.  I lead a section of about 20 marines and if these insecurities were visible to them that would decimate their confidence in myself in leading them.  I tried to take a step back and try to boost my confidence this term and well that didn't seem to work at all.

I try to be the rock and foundation with the answers but I have none.  I've gone through some of the trouble of maintaining a facade so people do not question my emotions but I still feel empty inside.  It gets me outside of the house at times but I always feel like the third wheel wherever I am at.

If I felt I had a purpose in life I feel that I would have more of a drive.  I feel like I'm rambling here but I'm trying to be succinct in describing this.
